description.value: The study investigated the neural correlates of forgiveness and unforgiveness during script-driven mental imagery of hurtful interpersonal scenarios in healthy volunteers using fMRI and effective connectivity analysis.

spans.text: In the present study, we used functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI) to investigate regional brain activity and cortical effective connectivity associated with forgiveness and unforgiveness.

model_settings.value: Pairwise Granger-causality analysis in frequency using a vector autoregressive model was applied to concatenated task-related ROI time series. description.value: Functional EPI volumes were concatenated across runs, motion-corrected and coregistered with 3dvolreg, temporally aligned with 3dTshift, spatially smoothed with a 4.5-mm FWHM kernel, and normalized within each run to percent signal change. Individual statistical maps were transformed to Talairach and Tournoux space and resampled to 1-mm voxels; a low-pass filter of 0–0.12 Hz was additionally applied for effective-connectivity analysis.

spans.text: script-driven mental imagery

description.value: Subjects imagined social scenarios describing emotionally hurtful events followed by instructions to forgive or unforgive the imagined offenders.

spans.text: Volunteers were engaged in script-driven mental imagery of personal offense, and subsequently instructed to either grant forgiveness to their imagined offender, or to fuel resentment and/or imagine revenge.
pre-hurtful condition

description.value: A neutral social scene presented before the offense; participants read and imagined the scenario without the hurtful event, providing a preparatory neutral condition.

spans.text: hurtful condition

description.value: A short narrative describing an emotionally hurtful interpersonal event caused by an imagined significant other; participants read and vividly imagined the offense and its emotional impact.

spans.text: Scenarios for the hurtful condition consisted of short stories adapted from the Willingness to Forgive Scale
forgiving response
The indication to forgive or to unforgive the offender were presented in a randomized way for all volunteers

description.value: Following the hurtful event, participants were instructed to forgive the imagined offender using one of four scenario-specific benevolent reappraisal strategies: explaining the offender's distress, justifying the behavior, assigning some responsibility to the victim, or positively reevaluating the consequences.

spans.text: Indications to forgive were accompanied by one among the following four types of reappraisal-instructions selected on the basis of each specific scenario

While in the MRI scanner, subjects were presented with narrative scenarios devised to evoke three consecutive emotional conditions: a pre-hurtful condition, a hurtful condition, and a forgiving or an unforgiving response.
Indications for unforgiveness were associated with (1) statements emphasizing the victim's resentment and/or (2) incitements to seek revenge

description.value: Following the hurtful event, participants were instructed to remain unforgiving by emphasizing resentment and/or imagining or seeking revenge against the imagined offender.

spans.text: Indications for unforgiveness were associated with (1) statements emphasizing the victim's resentment and/or (2) incitements to seek revenge

stimuli.value: Written descriptions for each scenario were projected on a screen.

advance through the screens by button pressing

instructions.value: Participants read and imagined each narrative scenario at their own pace, advancing through screens by button press. They were instructed to follow randomized indications either to forgive the imagined offender using scenario-specific benevolent reappraisal instructions or to remain unforgiving by emphasizing resentment and/or imagining revenge.

spans.text: Before the beginning of the fMRI scanning session, volunteers were clearly instructed to follow the indications that would be provided with each scenario.
